Recap From Part 1
In the previous part, we learned that Authentication answers only one question:
“Who are you?”
If a user enters the correct email and password, the application confirms their identity.
That’s it.
The application now knows:
“This is Ram.”
But here’s the important question.
Should Ram be allowed to:

• Delete every user?

• View other people’s bank accounts?

• Change product prices?

• Access the Admin Dashboard?
Obviously not.
This is where Authorization begins.
What Is Authorization?
